sections.heading: Regular -er and -ir verbs
sections.body: *-er* and *-ir* verbs share one set of preterite endings.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
- For *-ir* verbs, *nosotros* is the same in present and preterite: *vivimos* = we live / we lived. For *-er* verbs it differs: *comemos* (we eat) vs. *comimos* (we ate).
- Stem-changing *-er* verbs do **not** change in the preterite: *volver → volví, volvió*; *entender → entendí, entendió*.
- When the stem ends in a vowel, *-ió* and *-ieron* become *-yó* and *-yeron*: *leer → leyó, leyeron*; *creer → creyó*; *oír → oyó*. The *tú, nosotros* forms take an accent: *leíste, leímos*.
- *Ver* has no accents in the preterite because its forms are one syllable: *vi, viste, vio, vimos, vieron*.

sections.heading: Useful verbs
sections.body:
*Salir* (*salí*, I went out / left), *conocer* (*conocí*, I met — for the first time!), *nacer* (*nací*, I was born), *decidir* (*decidí*), *escribir* (*escribí*), *recibir* (*recibí*), *perder* (*perdí*, I lost), *correr* (*corrí*), *abrir* (*abrí*), *aprender* (*aprendí*), *vender* (*vendí*), *beber* (*bebí*).

Note *conocer* in the preterite means "to meet": *Conocí a mi esposo en 2015.* (I met my husband in 2015.)

examples: Comí en casa de mi abuela.
I ate at my grandmother's house.
I lived in Chile for two years.
Last night we went out dancing.
Sí, lo vi con mis amigos.
Yes, I watched it with my friends.
Mi padre leyó la noticia en el periódico.
My father read the news in the newspaper.
They decided to sell the house.
Escribimos una carta a la empresa.
We wrote a letter to the company.
We came back home very late.
I learned a lot in class.
You drank a lot of coffee.
My son was born in May.
